svg.title: Hypoxemia worked out from the arterial blood gas: a normal alveolar-arterial gradient means too little oxygen reaches the alveoli (low inspired oxygen at altitude, or hypoventilation with a high PaCO2); a raised gradient means oxygen fails to cross into blood, sorted by diffusion capacity and imaging (diffusion limitation), the response to 100% oxygen (shunt) or neither (ventilation-perfusion mismatch, the commonest); a normal PaO2 with hypoxia suggests carbon monoxide

svg.text: Low O2 saturation: get an ARTERIAL gas. PaO2 < 80? Then: is the A-a GRADIENT normal?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: arterial (PaO2) and alveolar (PAO2) O2 · alveolar gas: PAO2 = PIO2 − PaCO2 / 0.8 (room air: 150 − 1.25 × PaCO2)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: alveolar-arterial (A-a) gradient = PAO2 − PaO2 · normal ≤ age / 4 + 4 · a venous gas does not help

svg.text: A-a gradient NORMAL: too little O2 REACHES the alveoli

svg.text: A-a gradient RAISED: O2 fails to CROSS into the blood

svg.text: the problem is in the lung or its circulation
